source.title: DPN-LE: Dual Personality Neuron Localization and Editing for Large Language Models
source.authors: Lifan Zheng; Xue Yang; Jiawei Chen; Chenyan Wu; Jingyuan Zhang; Fanheng Kong; Xinyi Zeng; Xiang Chen; Yu Tian

record.tranche_reason: The study's own activation analysis argues that some neurons are multifunctional, refining the broad claim that neurons have a single job. It does not estimate the share of single-job neuron poles.
record.gate_note: The PCA analysis reports trait separation and says neurons in intersecting regions relate to both personality traits and general knowledge. This bears on neuron multifunctionality, but it is not an audit of named neuron-pole jobs or an out-of-sample test of explanations. Neuron counts, capability benchmarks, and editing results are not recorded as rows because they do not measure the proportion of poles with one job.
record.test_reason: This is a personality-editing method paper. Its one neuron-function statement is a qualitative reading of population-level PCA plots of MLP activations: intersecting regions are called multifunctional, linking traits and general knowledge. It does not audit individual neurons or poles, assign or count jobs, or score explanations. The study relies on neuron localization (trait-exclusive neurons) as a tool and reports mainly its own method's performance against NPTI and prompt baselines. None of its results bears on the single-job shares (V1/V2), the vision cases (V3/V4), attribution graphs (V5) or explanation-prediction tests (V6/V7).
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that existing neuron-editing methods (NPTI) modify many neurons unrelated to personality, which degrades general capability. They describe neurons as multifunctional and opposing traits as mutually exclusive in representation space. They propose DPN-LE, which selects about 0.5% of neurons by Cohen's d and activation magnitude, giving competitive personality control with better capability preservation.
record.recipe_differences: Uses contrastive personality samples and PCA of MLP activations to identify personality-related patterns; it does not use the original neuron-pole audit or test explanations on held-out activations.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported layer where personality separation emerges differs by model: layer 12 for LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct and layer 14 for Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct.

fits_no_version.finding: PCA of MLP activations separates high- and low-trait prompts from layer 12 (LLaMA) and layer 14 (Qwen). The authors describe neurons in intersecting regions as multifunctional, serving both personality and general knowledge. At the first separating layer, 21–50% of MLP neurons exceed |Cohen's d|>0.8 for a single trait (Table 7–8).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Personality-trait information is spread across a large fraction of mid/late MLP neurons in 7–8B instruct models. Many of these neurons also support general capabilities, so broad neuron editing degrades reasoning.

record.problems: The neuron-function evidence is based on activation contrasts and PCA, not a quantified audit of neuron jobs; no uncertainty estimates are reported for the finding relevant to this claim.
record.rows_left_out: Neuron-selection counts, personality-control scores, and general-capability outcomes are not included because they do not measure how many neuron poles have one or multiple jobs. The study also reports Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct activation separation, but does not report the intersecting-region multifunctionality result for that model.

untested.parts: No Qwen3-32B audit, no per-pole job assignment, no 90%/7%/2–4% shares.
No single-job shares across models, scale or MoE architectures. The models studied are LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, with personality steering only.
No vision models, InceptionV1 or recursive generalization.
No test of architecture, regularization or tools as causes of neuron messiness.
No attribution graphs or circuit explanations.
No test of whether explanations predict held-out firing.

record.verdict_notes: The record's 'tests/T5' with a V1 limits_scope label overreaches. The multifunctionality remark is qualitative, drawn from population PCA, and is not a neuron-level job audit, so no verdict is warranted. The Cohen's d counts (Tables 7–8) measure trait selectivity, not number of jobs. The capability-degradation tables concern the editing method, not neuron interpretability.

versions.untested_parts: Does not audit Qwen3-32B, count neuron poles by number of jobs, estimate the 90%/7%/2–4% shares, or test explanations on activations not used to write them.
Does not measure single-job shares across model sizes, dense and mixture-of-experts architectures, or models up to trillions of parameters.
Does not examine InceptionV1 or the cat-and-car neuron, pose, or recursive generalization.
Does not test the proposed causes of messy late-layer neurons or estimate interpretability shares for InceptionV1-sized vision models.
Does not evaluate attribution graphs or whether model behavior can be explained using the model's own neurons without a replacement model.
Does not test whether explanations fit activating examples but fail to predict activations on new examples.
Does not score neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.

rows.subject: LLaMA-3-8B-Instruct
rows.operation_detail: PCA analysis of MLP activations for high- and low-trait samples, with interpretation of intersecting activation regions
rows.measure: Activation-pattern separation and reported functions of neurons in intersecting regions
rows.value: Opposing traits form clearly separable clusters from layer 12; the study states that neurons in intersecting areas are multifunctional, relating to both personality traits and general knowledge.
rows.note: The reported multifunctionality qualifies a single-job account, but the study gives no count or share of multifunctional neurons and does not assign named jobs to neuron poles.
rows.check: PCA clustering of whole MLP activation vectors for high- versus low-trait prompts cannot show how many individual neurons or poles have one job. The multifunctionality statement is an unquantified interpretation with no per-neuron analysis behind it. It is not an audit of the V1 kind and does not involve Qwen3-32B, so it bears on no version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The study reports multifunctional neurons in intersecting regions, but does not measure how common they are; this qualifies the single-job claim without determining the claimed shares (r1).
